title: Weighted queue routing for tiered customers with quota-weight smoothing and fallback model variants
creator: Priya Shah
description: Goal: Implement a weighted queue-based tier routing layer that enforces per-customer/quota priorities across free, paid, and enterprise tiers, while performing graceful fallbacks to compatible model variants under capacity or quota constraints. The feature should enable predictable latency for enterprise commitments, lower priority smoothing for free users, and quota-aware preemption only when necessary. This ticket covers the routing algorithm, config schema, runtime admission controller, and necessary console visibility (per-tier queue health and evicted request logs).
acceptance_criteria: Routing policy supports three explicit tiers: free, paid, enterprise (configurable labels accepted)
Requests are placed into weighted queues; weights are configurable per-customer and per-route
Quota-aware prioritization decreases weight smoothly for over-quota tenants rather than abrupt dropping (leaky-bucket smoothing)
When capacity or latency SLOs are at risk, lower-weighted queues are throttled first; enterprise commitments should retain minimum throughput reserve
Model fallback happens automatically to pre-configured compatible variants (quantized / smaller model) with transparent reason codes returned in response metadata
Telemetry available: per-queue wait time, evictions, fallback rate, and per-tenant token usage at decision time
E2E tests simulate mixed loads from all three tiers and verify SLO preservation and predictable degradation patterns
No customer data is persisted in routing layer logs beyond telemetry aggregates (privacy check)
implementation_notes: Core algorithm: maintain per-tier token-buckets and an effective weight multiplier derived from (base_weight * quota_health_factor). Quota_health_factor = 1 for healthy, decreases towards 0.2 for progressive smoothing when tokens consumed > 90% of quota window.

Admission controller will run in the routing plane prior to model selection. If selected node lacks capacity, controller attempts fallback candidates in order (exact model -> quantized variant -> smaller architecture) until capacity found or failure.
Fallback decisions produce structured reason codes added to the response header (X-Redwood-Routing-Reason) and to console event logs.
Expose per-tenant weight override via Console (enterprise customers) and via API for advanced partners (RBAC-limited).
Config shape added to runtime: routing.tiers = [{name, base_weight, reserve_qps, fallback_list, quota_window_seconds}], plus global smoothing params.
Edge cases: for multi-region deployments, combine region affinity score into effective weight (region_score * tier_weight).
Backward compatibility: default behavior preserves current FIFO semantics by setting base_weight=1 and smoothing disabled unless config present.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (lab): unit + simulator tests against synthetic workloads (done)
Phase 1 (internal canary): route 5% of internal traffic through weighted queues for non-critical routes (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (customer pilot): enable for 3 paid customers + 1 enterprise with explicit opt-in; collect telemetry and SLOs (4 weeks)
Phase 3 (gradual ramp): toggle on default smoothing for free tier and configurable for paid (4 weeks), monitor metric thresholds before full rollout
Rollback: global feature flag to revert to FIFO routing within 15s; automated rollback if page-level SLO breaches occur
risks: Incorrect smoothing parameters could starve free users or unintentionally throttle paid traffic - mitigated by conservative defaults and staged canary
Complexity in multi-region affinity scoring could produce oscillations - mitigate with hysteresis and slower weight update cadence
Telemetry volume increase from per-decision logs - use aggregated counters and sampling
Misconfigured fallback chains could downgrade quality too aggressively - require opt-in per-route and automated golden prompt regressions
